newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. Fannie Mae targets Japanese investors.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Fannie Mae targets Japanese investors.

text.p: With cash-rich Japanese hungry for higher yields at a time of ultra-low domestic interest rates, the U.S. mortgage group Fannie Mae announced on Tuesday that it is targetting investors here.

Fannie Mae, formally called the Federal National Mortgage Association, is a U.S. government-sponsored group that purchases mortgages from banks and packages them for sale to individual investors. Its creation has sharply increased the mortgage money available to U.S. homebuyers.
The program in Japan is the first outside the United States.
"We're very well aware of (Japanese investors') appetite for higher-yielding investments in yen," James Johnson, chief executive officer at Fannie Mae, told Reuters.
"We're a very high-quality issuer...with great liquidity," Johnson said. "We're looking very carefully at increasing opportunities to issue in yen."
Fannie Mae said it was planning to develop the programme by early 1997.
At this stage, Fannie Mae is planning to offer Euroyen bonds, although the scale of the issue has not yet been decided, Linda Knight, senior vice president, told a news conference.
In June, Fannie Mae re-entered the yen bond market by issuing global bonds. Since then it has launched two yen-based issues, both in September.

Fannie Mae issues long-term debt to support its mortgage portfolio. At the current pace, it will issue approximately $80 billion to $85 billion worth of long-term debt in 1996. It plans to issue a similar volume of long-term debt in 1997.

Investors have been investing heavily in higher-yield yen-based bonds, especially those in the samurai and Euroyen markets, seeking higher returns. Japan's key interest rate has been at a record low of 0.5 percent for more than a year to bolster the nation's fragile economic recovery.
The yen-denominated samurai bond market, mainly targetting retail investors here, has boomed recently.
In the past couple of months, U.S. corporations including Walt Disney Co, McDonald's Corp, International Business Machines Corp, Ford Motor Co and PepsiCo Inc have launched samurai issues.
